questions.question: What are comparisons in Go, and how do they work?
questions.title: comparisons in Go: meaning and behaviour
questions.direct_answer: Go uses `==` and `!=` for equality and `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` for ordered values. Booleans, numbers, strings, pointers, and channels are comparable; arrays and structs are comparable only when every element or field is comparable. Slices, maps, and functions cannot be compared with each other using `==`; they can only be compared with `nil`. Interface equality depends on the dynamic value stored inside the interface.
